focus: Shared reference consistency and stale path families
noveltyJustification: Three findings are fully new (systemic legacy-path family across 8 shared files, phase-detection's two-surface and single-script staleness, inconsistent intra-shared link forms) and one is an ALREADY-ADOPTED verification of precedence, AGENTS.md pointer and ceiling-report resolution.
keyQuestions: Where is the shared layer internally inconsistent, stale or weak when each claim is checked against its callers and against how it loads?
ruledOut: Treat the stale paths as a routing bug - the router entries are correct; only prose inside referenced docs is stale
Report version skew among the shared files - the hub version authority deliberately stops at the hub root

label: Eight of the thirteen shared markdown files route readers through pre-merge directory families (references/webflow, references/opencode, references/motion_dev, assets/webflow, assets/universal) and none of those paths exists: the hub has no references/ dir, the only code-quality-checklist.md lives in sk-code-review/assets/, assets/universal/checklists/ is gone, and references/motion_dev/ is gone. 23 grep lines across 8 files, 22 of them path references in 7 files. Reproducing case: test -f on assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md fails while sk-code-review/assets/code-quality-checklist.md exists. NEW P1.

phase-detection.md is semantically stale beyond its dead paths: it says 'Both supported surfaces follow the same lifecycle' while the hub carries three surfaces, its per-phase tables list only WEBFLOW and OPENCODE, and its OPENCODE verification row names verify_alignment_drift.py alone while the live completion gate is the three-guard umbrella scripts/run-all-drift-guards.sh. Reproducing case: rg -n OBSIDIAN on phase-detection.md exits 1 while stack-detection.md counts several. NEW P1.

Cross-links inside the shared tier use three different forms for the same directory: stack-detection.md:154 links 'references/phase-detection.md' while its own sibling phase-detection.md links './stack-detection.md' correctly, and code-quality-standards.md:172 links bare 'references/universal/code-style-guide.md'. From stack-detection.md's directory the first link resolves to shared/references/references/phase-detection.md, which does not exist; no checker validates links inside referenced docs. Reproducing case: rg -n 'references/phase-detection.md' on stack-detection.md prints line 154. NEW P2.

Verified as already consistent: the precedence order OPENCODE > OBSIDIAN > WEBFLOW > UNKNOWN is identical in stack-detection.md:39, code-quality-standards.md:56 and hub SKILL.md:135; the AGENTS.md section 3 restraint-table pointer resolves (AGENTS.md:198); and the ceiling: harvest endpoint named by the style guide exists at sk-code-quality/scripts/ceiling-report.sh. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

direction: Treat the stale paths as a routing bug
reason: The router's own entries are correct; only prose inside referenced docs is stale. The fix class is a link sweep, not a router change.

direction: Report version skew among the shared files
reason: The hub's version-authority statement stops at the hub root; shared files carry independent versions by design.
